capabilities: Hide files and folders from the file explorer without moving them
Auto-shelve files by case-insensitive wildcard rules on file names
Focus the tree on a selected set of folders and files
Save and recall named focus sets
Batch shelve or restore items from a management panel
extras: Warns that wildcard rules can over-match (e.g. *hub also catches github); states no network access or telemetry; includes a regression test suite; supports Chinese and English UI; beta builds available via BRAT.
intentEvidence: Quiet Shelf does two things, both purely at the display layer of the file explorer.
motivation: The author sees the explorer as a browse surface, not an archive: "The file explorer is a browse surface, not an archive."
problem: Obsidian's file explorer shows every folder, so in large vaults finished notes crowd out the working set unless users reorganize their folder structure.

relations.evidence: Beta builds: add yunmin311/quiet-shelf-obsidian to BRAT.

summary: File explorer filter that hides archived and index notes from the tree and narrows the view to selected folders, without moving any files.
